::: {.key-question}
What chronic health conditions are experienced by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander peoples in the NEPHU catchment?
:::

## All Lung Conditions

### Self-Reported Lung Conditions

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Lung conditions, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
lung_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Health_Lung_LGA.csv",
                              variable = "lung") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(lung != "Not stated")

# Data wrangling
lung_lga <- lung_lga %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(lung = dplyr::case_when(
    lung == "Has a lung condition (including COPD and emphysema)" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = lung,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "yes")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Lung conditions, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
lung_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Health_Lung_AgeSex.csv",
                                    variable = "lung") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(lung != "Not stated")

# Data wrangling
lung_agesex <- lung_agesex %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(lung = dplyr::case_when(
    lung == "Has a lung condition (including COPD and emphysema)" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>%  
  #
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = lung,
                          dichot   = "yes")
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 2.2% (n = 249) of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have a lung condition. This was higher than for non-Indigenous people living in the NEPHU catchment (1.3%).

- The number of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have a lung condition ranged from 39 (Darebin and Whittlesea LGAs) to 0 (Manningham LGA).

- The gap between the observed number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have a lung condition and the number expected if the rate was the same as for non-Indigenous people was biggest for Darebin and Whittlesea LGAs.

- The percentage of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have a lung condition ranged from 2.8% (Darebin and Maroondah LGAs) to 0.0% (Manningham LGA).

- The number of people who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have a lung condition was highest for people aged 50-59 or 60-69 years for both males and females, and the percentage of people who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have a lung condition increased with increasing age for both genders.

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following question was asked of all people completing the ABS Census 2021.

- Has the person been told by a doctor or nurse that they have any of these long-term health conditions? (Select all that apply)
  - Arthritis
  - Asthma
  - Cancer (including remission)
  - Dementia (including Alzheimer's)
  - Diabetes (excluding gestational diabetes)
  - Heart disease (including heart attack or angina)
  - Kidney disease
  - Lung condition (including COPD or emphysema)
  - Mental health condition (including depression or anxiety)
  - Stroke
  - Any other long-term health condition(s)
  - No long-term health condition

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

### Hospital Admissions

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hospitalisations - lung conditions
# Data from PHIDU Social Health Atlas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in PHIDU data
hospital_lung <- f_read_phidu_iare_hospital(data_sheet    = "Admissions_principal_diag",
                                            column_select = "admissions_for_respiratory_system_diseases_aboriginal_people")

# Data wrangling
hospital_lung <- hospital_lung %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(iare_name = factor(iare_name, levels = iare_inc_vic_lvl)) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(iare_name)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [PHIDU Social Health Atlas](https://phidu.torrens.edu.au/social-health-atlases).

- During the four-year period 01 July 2017 to 30 June 2021 there were 2,694 hospital admissions for respiratory system diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne.

- The number of admissions for respiratory system diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 402 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 16 (Whitehorse IARE).

- The age-standardised rate of admissions for respiratory system diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 2,490 per 100,000 population (Maroondah IARE) to 692 per 100,000 population (Whitehorse IARE).

- 5 of the 10 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area had an age-standardised admission rate for respiratory system diseases above the average rate for all Australian Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Maroondah, Melbourne/Port Phillip, Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea, Craigieburn/Sunbury, and Moreland/Broadmeadows IAREs).

::: {.callout-tip title="ICD-10-AM codes and definitions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
Admissions for respiratory system diseases are defined as those with a principal diagnosis code in the following list, coded using the [International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision Australian Modification (ICD-10-AM)](https://www.ihacpa.gov.au/health-care/classification/icd-10-amachiacs):

  - J00-J06: Acute upper respiratory infections
  - J09-J18: Influenza and pneumonia
  - J20-J22: Other acute lower respiratory infections
  - J30-J39: Other diseases of upper respiratory tract
  - J40-J47: Chronic lower respiratory diseases
  - J60-J70: Lung diseases due to external agents
  - J80-J84: Other respiratory diseases principally affecting the interstitium
  - J85-J86: Suppurative and necrotic conditions of lower respiratory tract
  - J90-J94: Other diseases of pleura
  - J95-J99: Other diseases of the respiratory system

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

### Emergency Presentations

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Emergency presentations - lung conditions
# Data from PHIDU Social Health Atlas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in PHIDU data
emergency_lung <- f_read_phidu_iare_hospital(data_sheet    = "ED_total",
                                             column_select = "emergency_department_presentations_total_presentations_for_diseases_of_the_respiratory_system_aboriginal_people")

# Data wrangling
emergency_lung <- emergency_lung %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(iare_name = factor(iare_name, levels = iare_inc_vic_lvl)) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(iare_name)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [PHIDU Social Health Atlas](https://phidu.torrens.edu.au/social-health-atlases).

- Between 01 July 2019 and 30 June 2020 there were 1,073 emergency department presentations for respiratory system diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne.

- The number of emergency department presentations for respiratory system diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 156 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 29 (Melbourne East IARE).

- The age-standardised rate of emergency department presentations for respiratory system diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 4,211 per 100,000 population (Melbourne/Port Phillip IARE) to 2,211 per 100,000 population (Yarra Ranges IARE).

- 4 of the 9 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area with data available for reporting had an age-standardised rate of emergency department presentations for respiratory system diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people above the average for all Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Melbourne/Port Phillip, Maroondah, Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea, and Melbourne North-East IAREs).

::: {.callout-tip title="ICD-10-AM codes and definitions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
Emergency department presentations for respiratory system diseases are defined as those with a principal diagnosis code in the following list, coded using the [International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision Australian Modification (ICD-10-AM)](https://www.ihacpa.gov.au/health-care/classification/icd-10-amachiacs):

  - J00-J06: Acute upper respiratory infections
  - J09-J18: Influenza and pneumonia
  - J20-J22: Other acute lower respiratory infections
  - J30-J39: Other diseases of upper respiratory tract
  - J40-J47: Chronic lower respiratory diseases
  - J60-J70: Lung diseases due to external agents
  - J80-J84: Other respiratory diseases principally affecting the interstitium
  - J85-J86: Suppurative and necrotic conditions of lower respiratory tract
  - J90-J94: Other diseases of pleura
  - J95-J99: Other diseases of the respiratory system

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::
